items.item: The cover and six overviews implement the written typography, palette and illustration specification as one publication system.
Overview content hierarchy, grid, labels, observation questions and navigation remain consistent across the six species.
The details and comparisons share the publication's grid, annotation language, layout colours and ink-and-wash treatment while allowing enlarged explanatory views.
Bird and flower extensions preserve the diagnostic colours and structures of their supplied overview sources.
Every detail names its overview pair, and both comparisons identify their two source pairs without altering the fixed page plan.
The three method spreads, index and forms use the specified typography, grid, layout palette and applicable fixed labels.
The blank and worked forms retain identical field positions, with separate observation and question responses.
All method and record pages agree on the ordered observation process, adult accompaniment and leaving living subjects in place.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Where illustrations appear, they show independently composed natural subjects with visible ink marks and transparent colour washes. Simplified incidental texture and different poses or crops are acceptable; photographs substituted for commissioned illustrations, opaque rendering throughout, or invented diagnostic anatomy fail. An index or form need not contain an illustration.

Assess each depicted supplied species against its relevant features. Adult robin: orange-red face and breast, brown back, pale belly. Adult blue tit: blue cap and wings, white face with dark eye stripe, greenish back, yellow underparts and fine short beak; its overview shows it resting on a twig. Daisy: white rays and yellow centre on a slender stalk connected to a rooted low rosette of spoon-shaped leaves. Clover: an intact leaf normally has three leaflets joined at one point, beside a rounded white or pinkish head; pale markings may vary. Adult ladybird: red wing cases with three black spots on each side and one shared near the front, plus black-and-white thorax markings. Snail: mottled coiled shell attached to its body and two long upper tentacles; lower tentacles can be small or hidden. Detail crops may isolate the named feature, and natural occlusion is allowed; the ladybird overview must still communicate the seven-spot arrangement. Unrelated plants in reference backgrounds must not become daisy anatomy.

Reader-facing language and activities suit children aged 8–12 with adults, and depicted outings fit brief daytime observation in English town parks or gardens. Broader seasonal species facts and nighttime snail behaviour may be explained without changing the activity setting. Foreign reference-photo locations must not be presented as the book's outing locations, and the six subjects must remain possible encounters rather than guaranteed sightings.

The cover visibly carries the required title, subtitle and age label and an original illustration of one or more supplied species. Its typography, layout palette and illustration treatment implement the preceding specification; the depicted species retains its supplied diagnostic appearance.

Require European robin / Erithacus rubecula on 4–5, Blue tit / Cyanistes caeruleus on 6–7, Common daisy / Bellis perennis on 8–9, White clover / Trifolium repens on 10–11, 7-spot ladybird / Coccinella septempunctata on 12–13, and Garden snail / Cornu aspersum on 14–15. Every overview supplies three concise facts faithful to its species notes, at least two labels connected to the actual named structures, and one question retaining the supplied prompt's meaning. Definitions sit beside unfamiliar terms at first use. Wording of facts and prompts may change; names, assignments and biological meaning may not.

Each artwork reads as two facing portrait pages in the nominal 148:210 page proportion, with two text columns per page and a visible grid consistent with 66 mm columns, a 4 mm gap, 6 mm outer margins and a 6 mm protected band on each side of the central fold. Text, labels and diagnostic features stay outside protected bands; background washes may enter them. Judge relative geometry rather than exact raster dimensions. Both assigned folios appear on their corresponding pages: method 2–3, overviews 4–15 in species order, details 16–27 in the same order, bird comparison 28–29, flower comparison 30–31, places 32–33, questions 34–35, index 36–37, blank record 38–39 and worked record 40–41.

Typography, rules, panels and other layout elements use the specified dark green, pale green and rust system, with all three present on the tier-6 overview, index and blank-record spreads. Allow substrate white, transparency, antialiasing and small reproduction shifts. Natural organism colours are independent of the three layout inks. Substituting a different layout palette or recolouring diagnostic organism patches to match it fails.

Read the index as a complete navigation record headed Find a neighbour. It must pair European robin / Erithacus rubecula with 4–5; Blue tit / Cyanistes caeruleus with 6–7; Common daisy / Bellis perennis with 8–9; White clover / Trifolium repens with 10–11; 7-spot ladybird / Coccinella septempunctata with 12–13; and Garden snail / Cornu aspersum with 14–15. Both 36 and 37 are printed. Ordering and visual grouping may vary, but missing, duplicated or misassociated entries fail, including omission of species without delivered overviews in tier 6.

The two-page specification functions as the upstream design specification and explicitly states the exact title and subtitle, ages 8–12, #24352A, #DCE5C9, #AD5B3C, 148 × 210 mm pages, two columns per page, 4 mm column gaps, and 6 mm outer margins and safe bands on both sides of the fold. It names actual typefaces rather than generic categories, defines the overview name/three-fact/two-label/question pattern, records the six species' supplied diagnostic features, and gives Pause → Notice → Record plus I noticed, I wonder and Not seen. Choices left open by the commission may vary; omissions or contradictions of fixed specifications fail.

Compare each artwork with the written specification for applicable typography, colour roles, illustration treatment, reader age, content pattern and page geometry. Spread geometry applies to interior spreads; the cover applies the identity and illustration rules. Reflow and subject-specific compositions may vary within the specified system. Material contradictions between the specification and applications fail.

The presentation explicitly repeats the specification's 148 × 210 mm page size, two columns per page, 4 mm gap, 6 mm outer margins and fold bands, ages 8–12, all three exact colour codes and actual typeface names. These facts may appear in a legible reused specification or explanatory text. Implicit visual resemblance, generic type categories, omitted values or inconsistent numbers fail.

Every target visibly presents the three method labels in the required reading order and reinforces quiet adult-accompanied observation from an accessible path or permitted garden, leaving living subjects in place. The introductory method spread explains the steps through a daytime scene. Both records use the exact observation, question and absence labels and distinguish observations from questions or possible explanations. Layout and reminder wording may vary; reordered steps or instructions to disturb subjects fail.

The blank and completed spreads use the same field positions for place, date/time, weather, visible features, sketch, behaviour and uncertainty. Above the worked data, print Practice example — not a field record. Preserve all supplied values: 17 May 2027, 10:20; Practice garden path (invented); Overcast after rain; White clover / Trifolium repens; One leaf had three visible leaflets with pale markings; Sketch one leaf with three leaflets; No movement noticed while looking at the leaf; I could see three leaflets on this one leaf; Are there flower heads hidden by the grass?; Other leaves were partly covered; I did not count them. Keep the observation and question responses in their respective fields. Wrapping is flexible; changes to data, missing values or a redesigned worked form fail.

Each detail visibly develops its own delivered overview, preserving diagnostic colours and structures while permitting enlargement, new explanatory panels and different scale. Require robin face/breast/back/belly on 16–17 linked to 4–5; blue tit cap/eye stripe on 18–19 linked to 6–7; daisy head and rooted rosette, including a diagram of the two flower types, on 20–21 linked to 8–9; clover joined leaflets and rounded head on 22–23 linked to 10–11; a complete ladybird top view with three spots per wing case and one shared front spot on 24–25 linked to 12–13; and snail shell and tentacles on 26–27 linked to 14–15. Every spread prints Detail and its source overview pair. Missing developments, mismatched sources or incorrect structures fail.

The bird spread places the delivered robin and blue tit subjects into a comparison of their face and colour clues, with folios 28–29 and references 4–5 and 6–7. The flower spread compares the delivered daisy and clover leaf and flower structures, with folios 30–31 and references 8–9 and 10–11. Repositioning, resizing and comparison annotations are allowed; changing diagnostic features, substituting unrelated subjects or omitting either source pair fails.

The places spread gives usable guidance for accessible paths and gardens where observation is permitted. The questions spread addresses all six supplied prompt meanings: robin perch and movement during a sketch; blue tit recognition through two colour areas; daisy leaf position relative to its head; clover visible versus hidden attached leaflets; visible ladybird spots and uncertainty about hidden spots; and snail extended versus sheltered parts after rain. It separates things observed from questions or explanations. Paraphrasing and grouping are allowed; omitted prompts, conflated evidence and speculation, or a different page assignment fail.

Review the full 10-second video against the delivered artwork. It visibly includes the cover, introductory method spread, every one of the six overviews, at least one delivered detail, both comparisons and a blank-to-worked record sequence. Any supplied detail may be selected; montage, motion and cropping are allowed if the required artwork remains identifiable. Missing page groups, newly substituted artwork or an indiscernible form progression fail.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least twelve pages and visibly reuses the specification and every delivered book artwork. Each of the six details appears with its own source overview in a clearly paired page or facing spread, and blank and worked records are presented together for comparison. Scaling and multi-artwork pages are allowed; omitted sources, incorrect detail pairings or merely naming an artwork without displaying it fail.

The cover and six overviews implement the written typography, palette and illustration specification as one publication system. Overview content hierarchy, grid, labels, observation questions and navigation remain consistent across the six species.

The details and comparisons share the publication's grid, annotation language, layout colours and ink-and-wash treatment while allowing enlarged explanatory views. Bird and flower extensions preserve the diagnostic colours and structures of their supplied overview sources. Every detail names its overview pair, and both comparisons identify their two source pairs without altering the fixed page plan.

The three method spreads, index and forms use the specified typography, grid, layout palette and applicable fixed labels. The blank and worked forms retain identical field positions, with separate observation and question responses. All method and record pages agree on the ordered observation process, adult accompaniment and leaving living subjects in place.
